Two population pyramids side by side. The left one (Developing Country, e.g., Nigeria) has a wide base that narrows sharply to the top, showing many young people and few old people. The right one (Developed Country, e.g., Japan) has a narrower base and a bulging middle, showing fewer young people and many middle-aged/elderly people. The horizontal axis shows percentage of population, the vertical axis shows age groups (0-4, 5-9, up to 80+), with males on the left (blue) and females on the right (pink). Clean flat textbook illustration, white background.

A simplified world map showing global population distribution. Dark shading indicates densely populated areas (e.g., North-Eastern USA, Western Europe, India, Eastern China). Light shading indicates sparsely populated areas (e.g., Sahara Desert, Amazon Basin in South America, Northern Canada, Australian Outback).

A conceptual diagram showing migration. On the left, a rural village (Source) with arrows pointing outward (poverty, lack of jobs, poor amenities, soil exhaustion). A large arrow points to the right, representing "Migration". On the right, a modern city skyline (Destination) with arrows pointing inward (jobs, electricity, hospitals, higher wages). Clean flat textbook illustration, white background.
